mainTopic: Vows with conditions that cannot work, and the argument between בית שמאי and בית הלל about סמיכה on holiday offerings.
overview: The amud opens with the end of a question ריש לקיש asked רבי יוחנן: what if someone becomes a נזיר but plans to pay for his offerings with מעשר שני money? The answer is that the vow holds but the plan does not work. A similar case follows. A man said, 'give 400 זוז to so-and-so and let him marry my daughter.' רב פפא rules that the man takes the money and the marriage is up to him, though putting the condition first would have made the gift depend on it. Next a ברייתא learns from a פסוק that an obligatory עולה needs סמיכה. רבי יצחק בר אבא says this fits only בית שמאי, but the גמרא shows it can fit בית הלל too, by learning obligatory שלמים from two sources together. The גמרא then brings two ברייתות that disagree about what בית שמאי and בית הלל actually argued over: סמיכה itself, or slaughtering right after it. Finally comes the story of הלל הזקן bringing his עולה on יום טוב, and of בבא בן בוטא, a student of שמאי who knew the הלכה follows בית הלל. His story continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Can a נזיר pay for his offerings with מעשר שני money?
steps.stepSummary: The end of ריש לקיש's question: someone says 'I am a נזיר, and I will shave using מעשר שני money.' What is the law?
steps.simpleTranslation: '...and I will shave with second-tithe money.' What is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the last words of a question already in progress. Someone accepted נזירות but said he would pay for the offerings at the end of it with מעשר שני money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעשר שני money must be spent on food eaten in ירושלים, and it is not meant for paying off a new obligation like a נזיר's offerings. So the question is whether this person's plan cancels his vow, makes the plan valid, or neither.

keyTerms.meaning: And I will shave. This is how a נזיר finishes his term, together with bringing his offerings.
Second tithe: produce or money that must be used for eating in ירושלים

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new question. It is the second half of a two-part question that started before this section, together with a case about a תודה and חגיגה.

phrases.english: and I will shave with second-tithe money, what is the law?
phrases.notes: The case starts earlier with 'I am a נזיר.' 'Shaving' here means buying and bringing the offerings that end the נזירות.

steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a vow of נזירות with a plan to pay from מעשר שני works, and whether that plan is allowed.

steps.title: The vow holds, but the condition does not work
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers: in the תודה case, the person is bound by his vow but does not fulfill his חגיגה obligation with it. In the נזיר case, he is a נזיר but may not use מעשר שני money for his shaving offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: He has vowed, but he does not fulfill his obligation. He is a נזיר, but he does not shave with that money.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers both parts of the question. In each case the main vow stands, and the extra plan attached to it is thrown out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person cannot escape his vow by attaching a plan that does not work. The obligation he took on holds in full, and the shortcut he wanted is simply not allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: He has vowed, so he is bound by the vow
But he does not fulfill his obligation
A נזיר, someone who vowed to avoid wine, haircuts, and contact with the dead

steps.whatToRemember: When a vow comes with a plan that cannot work, the vow stands and the plan is ignored.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the main idea of the section: one part of a statement can take effect while the attached condition does not. The next story builds on that.

phrases.english: He said to him: He has vowed, but he does not fulfill his obligation.
phrases.notes: This answers the first part of the question, about bringing a תודה and counting it as his חגיגה.

phrases.english: He is a nazirite, but he does not shave.
phrases.notes: He means he cannot shave and bring offerings paid for with the מעשר שני money.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The vow takes effect, but the attached condition (meeting the חגיגה obligation, or paying from מעשר שני) does not.

steps.title: A gift of 400 זוז with 'let him marry my daughter'
steps.stepSummary: A man instructed: 'Give 400 זוז to so-and-so, and let him marry my daughter.' רב פפא rules that the man takes the money, and marrying the daughter is up to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man said to them: Give four hundred זוז to so-and-so, and let him marry my daughter. רב פפא said: He takes the four hundred, and as for the daughter, if he wants he marries her, and if he wants he does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a similar case where a statement has two parts. רב פפא rules that the gift is final and the marriage is optional.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man first gave the money outright. Only afterward did he add 'let him marry my daughter,' so that was a wish, not a condition. Because the gift was complete before the wish was mentioned, the gift stands on its own.

keyTerms.meaning: And let him marry my daughter

phrases.english: A certain man who said to them:

phrases.aramaic: הַבוּ לֵיהּ אַרְבַּע מְאָה זוּזֵי לִפְלוֹנִי,
phrases.english: Give four hundred zuz to so-and-so,
and let him marry my daughter.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: אַרְבַּע מְאָה — שָׁקֵיל,
phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: The four hundred, he takes,
and his daughter: if he wants, he marries her,
if he wants, he does not marry her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel case: as in step 2, one part of the statement takes effect on its own.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the gift is stated before the request to marry, the recipient keeps the money whether or not he marries the daughter.

steps.title: Word order decides whether it is a condition
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that רב פפא's ruling depends on the gift being mentioned first. Had the man said 'let him marry, and give him,' the money would depend on the marriage.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason is that he said 'give him, and let him marry.' But if he said 'let him marry, and give him,' then if he marries he takes the money, and if he does not marry he does not take it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a lesson from the wording of the case. It shows that the order of the two parts changes the result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the marriage is mentioned first, the money is tied to it, so it is a true condition. If the gift is mentioned first, the gift is already complete, and the marriage becomes a mere suggestion.
steps.whatToRemember: Gift first, then the request: he keeps the money no matter what. Request first, then the gift: no marriage, no money.

phrases.english: The reason is that he said 'give him, and let him marry,'

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אִי אָמַר לִנְסֵיב וְהַבוּ לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: but if he said 'let him marry, and give him,'
if he marries, he takes,
and if he does not marry, he does not take.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows רב פפא's ruling to the case where the gift was mentioned first.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the condition comes before the gift, the gift depends on the condition being fulfilled.

steps.title: Who first taught this law
steps.stepSummary: מרימר taught this law in his own name. רבינא told him that in their tradition it is taught as ריש לקיש's question to רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: מרימר sat and taught this teaching in his own name. רבינא said to מרימר: You teach it this way, but we teach it as what ריש לקיש asked of רבי יוחנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story about who a teaching belongs to. רבינא corrects the credit for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The law itself is not changed here. רבינא points out that it was not מרימר's own idea, but came from the exchange between ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן in steps 1 and 2.

phrases.english: Mareimar sat and was saying this teaching
phrases.notes: 'This teaching' is the law about a vow with a condition attached, from steps 1 and 2.

phrases.english: in his own name.
Ravina said to Mareimar:
You teach it this way,
we teach it as what Reish Lakish asked
of Rabbi Yochanan, that is how we teach it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the question and answer of steps 1 and 2 to say who taught them.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The law about a vow with a condition attached is credited to the question ריש לקיש asked רבי יוחנן, not to מרימר.

steps.title: A ברייתא teaches that an obligatory burnt-offering needs leaning of hands
steps.stepSummary: A תנא recites a ברייתא before רבי יצחק בר אבא. Based on a פסוק, it teaches that an obligatory עולה needs סמיכה, just like a gift עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A תנא taught before רבי יצחק בר אבא: 'And he brought the burnt-offering and did it according to the regulation.' This means following the rules of a gift burnt-offering. It teaches that an obligatory burnt-offering also requires leaning hands on the animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא. It learns from a פסוק that an עולת חובה needs סמיכה, the same as an עולת נדבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'כַּמִּשְׁפָּט' (according to the regulation) points back to the known rules of a gift עולה. So whatever applies to the gift עולה, including סמיכה, also applies to the obligatory one. The key point for later is that this ברייתא needs a פסוק for this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: A gift burnt-offering that a person brings because he chooses to
A burnt-offering a person is required to bring
Leaning one's hands on the animal's head before it is slaughtered
According to the regulation, meaning following the set rules

phrases.aramaic: תָּנֵי תַּנָּא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר אַבָּא:
phrases.english: A tanna taught before Rabbi Yitzchak bar Abba:
phrases.notes: A תנא here is someone whose job was to memorize and recite ברייתות out loud.

phrases.english: "And he brought the burnt-offering
and did it according to the regulation"
like the regulation of a gift burnt-offering.
This teaches about an obligatory burnt-offering
that it requires leaning of hands.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי תַּנָּא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, the source for סמיכה on an obligatory עולה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An obligatory עולה requires סמיכה, learned from 'כַּמִּשְׁפָּט' comparing it to a gift עולה.

steps.title: רבי יצחק says this ברייתא follows בית שמאי
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק בר אבא says the ברייתא matches only בית שמאי. בית הלל learn obligatory offerings from gift offerings by logic, so they would not need a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The one who told you this, whose view is it? It is בית שמאי, who do not learn obligatory peace-offerings from gift peace-offerings. If it were בית הלל, who do learn obligatory peace-offerings from gift ones, then an obligatory burnt-offering would also not need a פסוק. They would learn it from a gift burnt-offering.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק answers the תנא. The ברייתא only works for בית שמאי, because for בית הלל a פסוק would not be needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל compare obligatory שלמים to gift שלמים for סמיכה. By the same logic, they would compare an obligatory עולה to a gift עולה with no פסוק. Since the ברייתא does need a פסוק, it must hold like בית שמאי, who do not make that comparison.

keyTerms.meaning: Peace-offerings a person is required to bring, such as on a holiday
Peace-offerings a person brings because he chooses to
They learn one case from another

steps.whyThisMatters: It ties a ברייתא about עולה to the well-known argument between בית שמאי and בית הלל about סמיכה.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: רבי יצחק בר אבא is speaking to the תנא.

phrases.english: The one who told you this, whose view is it?
It is Beit Shammai,
who do not learn obligatory peace-offerings
from gift peace-offerings.
For if it were Beit Hillel,

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דְּגָמְרִי שַׁלְמֵי חוֹבָה מִשַּׁלְמֵי נְדָבָה,
phrases.english: since they learn obligatory peace-offerings from gift peace-offerings,

phrases.aramaic: עוֹלַת חוֹבָה נָמֵי לָא תִּבְעֵי קְרָא,
phrases.english: an obligatory burnt-offering would also not need a verse,
since they would learn it from a gift burnt-offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: דַּאֲמַר לָךְ מַנִּי — בֵּית שַׁמַּאי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the ברייתא from step 6 to בית שמאי only
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ברייתא needing a פסוק fits בית שמאי. For בית הלל, an obligatory עולה would be learned from a gift עולה by logic.

steps.title: Maybe בית הלל learn from the obligatory burnt-offering instead
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions רבי יצחק's assumption. Maybe בית הלל learn obligatory שלמים from an obligatory עולה, and that עולה itself needs a פסוק. Then the ברייתא could fit בית הלל too.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know that בית הלל learn obligatory peace-offerings from gift peace-offerings? Maybe they learn them from an obligatory burnt-offering, and the obligatory burnt-offering itself needs a פסוק.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יצחק's reasoning. It suggests a different source for בית הלל's rule, which would let the ברייתא fit בית הלל as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יצחק assumed בית הלל compare obligatory to gift. The גמרא offers another option: they compare obligatory שלמים to an obligatory עולה. If so, the obligatory עולה still needs its own פסוק, which is the one in the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do we know?

phrases.english: And from where do we know that Beit Hillel
learn obligatory peace-offerings from gift peace-offerings?
Perhaps they learn them from an obligatory burnt-offering,
and the obligatory burnt-offering itself needs a verse.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִמַּאי דְּבֵית הִלֵּל שַׁלְמֵי חוֹבָה מִשַּׁלְמֵי נְדָבָה גָּמְרִי
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יצחק's claim that בית הלל learn obligatory שלמים from gift שלמים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another source is possible, the obligatory עולה. That would leave room for a פסוק even according to בית הלל.

steps.title: The suggestion fails because the burnt-offering is entirely burnt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on the suggestion. If gift שלמים can't be the source because they are common, then an obligatory עולה can't be the source either, because it is entirely burnt. The next step answers this.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why would they not learn from gift peace-offerings? Because those are common. Then they should also not learn from an obligatory burnt-offering, because it is entirely burnt!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the suggestion from step 8. Each possible source has a difference from obligatory שלמים, so the obligatory עולה is no better a source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only reason not to learn from gift שלמים would be that they are common, and common offerings might have their own rules. But an obligatory עולה also has a difference: it is completely burned on the מזבח, unlike שלמים, which are eaten. Since neither source is a perfect match on its own, there seems to be no reason to prefer the obligatory עולה. Step 10 answers this by combining the two sources.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי שְׁנָא מִשַּׁלְמֵי נְדָבָה דְּלָא גָּמְרִי —
phrases.english: What is different, that they do not learn from gift peace-offerings?
Because they are common.
phrases.notes: Gift offerings come often, so you might think they have special rules of their own.

phrases.english: Then they should also not learn from an obligatory burnt-offering,
because it is entirely burnt!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא מִשַּׁלְמֵי נְדָבָה דְּלָא גָּמְרִי — שֶׁכֵּן מְצוּיִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the alternative proposed in step 8
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that בית הלל learn obligatory שלמים from an obligatory עולה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The obligatory עולה has its own difference, being כליל. So it is no better a source than gift שלמים, which differ only in being common.

steps.title: Learning obligatory peace-offerings from both sources together
steps.stepSummary: Obligatory שלמים are learned from a combination of gift שלמים and an obligatory עולה. So the ברייתא could fit בית הלל too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is learned from between the two of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the rejection in Step 9. It does not learn from just one source. It combines two sources together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each source has a weak point on its own. An obligatory עולה is entirely burnt, and gift שלמים are common. But gift שלמים are not entirely burnt, and an obligatory עולה is not common. So together they show that obligatory שלמים need סמיכה. This means בית הלל might still need a פסוק for the obligatory עולה, so רבי יצחק בר אבא's proof that the ברייתא fits only בית שמאי falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: It comes, meaning it is learned
From between them, meaning from combining two sources

steps.confusionAlert: This step does not prove that רבי יצחק בר אבא is wrong about the halacha. It only shows that his proof from the ברייתא is not forced, because the ברייתא could fit בית הלל too.

phrases.english: (Rather,) it is derived from between the two of them.
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets. 'The two of them' means gift שלמים and the obligatory עולה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 9 and brings back the possibility raised in Step 8, that the ברייתא fits בית הלל.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Each source alone can be rejected, so בית הלל would need no פסוק.
steps.terutzMaskana: The two sources together teach obligatory שלמים. So the פסוק for the obligatory עולה is still needed, even for בית הלל.

steps.title: Do בית שמאי really hold that obligatory peace-offerings need no hand-placing?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא of רבי יוסי says both sides agree that סמיכה is needed. They only argue about whether the slaughter must come right after the סמיכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do בית שמאי really hold that obligatory peace-offerings need no סמיכה? But a ברייתא teaches that רבי יוסי said: בית שמאי and בית הלל did not argue about whether סמיכה itself is needed. Everyone agrees that it is. They argued about whether slaughter must come right after סמיכה. בית שמאי say this is not needed, and בית הלל say it is.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the basic assumption that בית שמאי hold obligatory שלמים need no סמיכה. It brings a ברייתא that says otherwise.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יוסי, both sides agree that סמיכה is required. Their argument is only about timing. בית שמאי allow the סמיכה to be done earlier, such as before יום טוב. בית הלל require the slaughter to follow right after the סמיכה. This contradicts the claim that בית שמאי do not require סמיכה at all.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא? This phrase opens a challenge.
Pressing one's hands on the animal's head before it is slaughtered
Slaughter must come immediately after סמיכה

phrases.english: And do Beit Shammai hold
that obligatory peace-offerings do not require placing of hands?
But isn't it taught: Rabbi Yosei said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל
phrases.english: Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel did not disagree
about the placing of hands itself, that it is required.
About what did they disagree?
About whether slaughter must come immediately after placing hands.
For Beit Shammai say: it is not necessary.
And Beit Hillel say: it is necessary!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסָבְרִי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי שַׁלְמֵי חוֹבָה לָא בָּעוּ סְמִיכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the proof question to challenge what בית שמאי actually hold.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that בית שמאי hold obligatory שלמים need no סמיכה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא of רבי יוסי says both sides agree that סמיכה is required. The only argument is about timing.

steps.title: Following a different תנא who reports the argument the other way
steps.stepSummary: The view that בית שמאי require no סמיכה follows רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה. He says the argument is about סמיכה itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said it in line with this תנא. A ברייתא teaches that רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה said: בית שמאי and בית הלל did not argue about whether slaughter must come right after סמיכה. Everyone agrees that it must. They argued about סמיכה itself. בית שמאי say it is not needed, and בית הלל say it is.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. There are two traditions about what the argument was, and our view follows the second one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה flips רבי יוסי's version. In his version, the timing rule is agreed on, and the real argument is whether obligatory שלמים need סמיכה at all. So the view that בית שמאי require no סמיכה is backed by a תנא, and the challenge is answered.

keyTerms.meaning: רבי יוסי, son of רבי יהודה

steps.whatToRemember: There are two versions of the בית שמאי–בית הלל argument. In רבי יוסי's version, they argue about timing. In רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's version, they argue about whether סמיכה is needed at all.

phrases.english: He said it in accordance with this tanna,
phrases.notes: In other words, whoever said בית שמאי require no סמיכה is following the next ברייתא.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה:
phrases.english: as it is taught: Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל
phrases.english: Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel did not disagree
about slaughter immediately after placing hands, that it is necessary.
About what did they disagree?
About the placing of hands itself.
For Beit Shammai say: it is not necessary,
and Beit Hillel say: it is necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from רבי יוסי's ברייתא in Step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Relying on a different תנא's version of the argument
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Everyone agrees that obligatory שלמים need סמיכה, as רבי יוסי says.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, בית שמאי do not require סמיכה. The view in question follows him.

steps.title: The story of הלל הזקן bringing his burnt-offering on a festival
steps.stepSummary: הלל הזקן brought his עולה to the עזרה on יום טוב to do סמיכה. When the students of שמאי questioned him, he avoided an argument and they left.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: There was a story about הלל הזקן. He brought his עולה to the עזרה to do סמיכה on it on יום טוב. The students of שמאי הזקן gathered around him and asked: What kind of animal is this? He said: It is a female, and I brought it as a שלמים. He swung its tail for them, and they went away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the main argument between בית שמאי and בית הלל. It brings a ברייתא with a story showing הלל acting on his view on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הלל brought an עולה to do סמיכה on יום טוב, which בית שמאי do not allow. To keep the peace, he answered that it was a female brought as a שלמים. A female could not be an עולה. He swung the tail, so the students could not check, and they left without a fight.

keyTerms.meaning: The courtyard of the בית המקדש
What is its nature, meaning what kind of animal is it

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
There was an incident with Hillel the Elder,
who brought his burnt-offering to the Temple courtyard
to place his hands on it on a Festival.
The students of Shammai the Elder gathered around him

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: מָה טִיבָהּ שֶׁל בְּהֵמָה זוֹ?
phrases.english: and said to him: What is the nature of this animal?
He said to them: It is a female,
phrases.notes: An עולה must be a male, so calling it a female means it can't be an עולה.

phrases.english: and I brought it as a peace-offering.
He swung its tail for them,
and they went away.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the main argument between בית שמאי and בית הלל through a story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הלל brought an עולה for סמיכה on יום טוב. He kept the peace with שמאי's students by not arguing with them.

steps.title: בית שמאי gain the upper hand and try to fix the הלכה
steps.stepSummary: On that day בית שמאי were stronger than בית הלל, and they wanted to set the הלכה according to their own view.
steps.simpleTranslation: And on that day, בית שמאי had the upper hand over בית הלל, and they wanted to establish the הלכה like their opinion.
steps.whatsHappening: The story keeps going. The גמרא tells us that on that day בית שמאי were stronger and tried to make the הלכה follow them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the last step, הלל avoided an argument with the students of שמאי, and they left. Now we learn that on that day בית שמאי were the stronger group and wanted to use that moment to fix the הלכה their way. This sets up the danger that the next part of the story will deal with.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'their hand grew strong'; they had the upper hand
To fix or establish the הלכה as final

phrases.english: And on that day

phrases.aramaic: גָּבְרָה יָדָם שֶׁל בֵּית שַׁמַּאי עַל בֵּית הִלֵּל,
phrases.english: the hand of בית שמאי grew stronger than בית הלל,
and they wanted to fix the הלכה like them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאוֹתוֹ הַיּוֹם גָּבְרָה יָדָם שֶׁל בֵּית שַׁמַּאי עַל בֵּית הִלֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of הלל הזקן from step 13 by telling what happened afterward on that same day.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On that day בית שמאי had the upper hand and tried to fix the הלכה according to their view.

steps.title: בבא בן בוטא, a student of שמאי who knew the הלכה follows בית הלל
steps.stepSummary: An elder named בבא בן בוטא, from the students of שמאי הזקן, knew the הלכה follows בית הלל, and he sent for something; the story continues next.
steps.simpleTranslation: And there was a certain elder there, from the students of שמאי הזקן, named בבא בן בוטא, who knew that the הלכה follows בית הלל, and he sent...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא introduces a new person in the story, בבא בן בוטא, who knew the הלכה follows בית הלל. The sentence stops at 'and he sent', so the גמרא is setting up his action in the next part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though בבא בן בוטא was a student of שמאי, he knew the הלכה here follows בית הלל. That makes him the one who can stop בית שמאי from fixing the הלכה their way. What he sent for is not told yet; it comes in the next part.

keyTerms.meaning: An elder; a senior Torah scholar
שמאי the Elder, the teacher of בית שמאי
An elder from the students of שמאי

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix him up with בית שמאי's side. He was a student of שמאי, but he knew the הלכה in this case follows בית הלל.

phrases.english: And there was a certain elder there
from the students of שמאי the Elder,
and בבא בן בוטא was his name,
who knew that the הלכה follows בית הלל,
and he sent

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָיָה שָׁם זָקֵן אֶחָד מִתַּלְמִידֵי שַׁמַּאי הַזָּקֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces the person who will respond to בית שמאי's attempt in step 14 to fix the הלכה their way.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בבא בן בוטא, a student of שמאי הזקן, knew the הלכה follows בית הלל and took action, which the story goes on to describe.
